slice.leaf: rmcp Streamable HTTP authenticated-principal bridge: prove exact-release Axum middleware ordering relative to StreamableHttpService
slice.finding: The exact rmcp-v3.1.4 release example constructs StreamableHttpService, nests it at /mcp, then applies axum middleware::from_fn_with_state(auth_middleware) to that protected router. auth_middleware receives the full http Request<Body> and only reaches rmcp by calling next.run(request). Therefore authentication middleware is structurally upstream of the rmcp service for this supported composition, and it has the standard Request extension mutation surface before forwarding. Combined only with this role's prior source-qualified finding that rmcp captures http::request::Parts into RequestContext extensions, the safe principal bridge is: trusted middleware authenticates, inserts Principal into Request.extensions, forwards, and the tool reads RequestContext.extensions -> Parts.extensions; missing Principal must fail closed.
slice.scope_limit: This slice proves the supported Axum/Tower placement and ordering using the exact release example. It does not claim that the example itself inserts a Principal, does not prove any particular authentication scheme, and does not prove persistent task create-or-get, restart redrive, or external-effect exactly-once safety.
slice.quota_zero_assessment: The composition is local in-process middleware plus lightweight request handling; it does not require hosted runners, Codespaces, artifact/LFS/package quotas, cloud credits, or external model/API credits.
